ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a billboard CD stands on top of a building. Xiao Ming and his classmates measured the angle of elevation to the bottom of the billboard, D, as $53^\circ$ from point A at the foot of the hill. Walking up the slope AB to point B, they measured the angle of elevation to the top of the billboard, C, as $45^\circ$. It is known that the slope of the hill, AB, has a gradient of $i=1\colon \sqrt{3}$ and $AB=12$ meters, $AE=24$ meters. (The height of the protractor is negligible, and the result should be accurate to 0.1 meter, reference data: $\sqrt{2}\approx 1.41$, $\sqrt{3}\approx 1.73$, $\sin 53^\circ\approx \frac{4}{5}$, $\cos 53^\circ\approx \frac{3}{5}$, $\tan 53^\circ\approx \frac{4}{3}$). How tall is the billboard CD, in meters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In right triangle $ABM$,\\
$\therefore NE=BM=\frac{1}{2}AB=6$ (meters),\\
$AM=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}AB=6\sqrt{3}$ (meters),\\
$\therefore ME=AM+AE=\left(6\sqrt{3}+24\right)$ meters,\\
$\because \angle CBN=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore CN=BN=ME=\left(6\sqrt{3}+24\right)$ meters,\\
$\therefore CE=CN+NE=\left(6\sqrt{3}+30\right)$ meters,\\
In right triangle $ADE$, $\angle DAE=53^\circ$, $AE=24$ meters,\\
$\therefore DE=AE\cdot\tan53^\circ\approx 24\times \frac{4}{3}=32$ (meters),\\
$\therefore CD=CE-DE$\\
$=6\sqrt{3}+30-32$\\
$=6\sqrt{3}-2$\\
$\approx \boxed{8.4}$ (meters)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows a building on the right with vertical side EC. A billboard segment CD is on top of the building, with D the bottom of the billboard and C the top. Point A is on the horizontal ground to the left of E, and AE is the ground distance to the building. A sloped hillside segment AB rises up to point B on the left. The line of sight from A to D is marked with an elevation angle of 53°, and the line of sight from B to C is marked with an elevation angle of 45°. Reasoning following the assigned construction: Draw a vertical from B down to the ground line at M, and draw a horizontal from B to the building vertical EC at N. Since the hill gradient is i = 1:√3, the vertical rise and horizontal run along AB are in the ratio 1:√3. With AB = 12, triangle ABM has side proportions 1:√3:2, so BM = 12 × 1/2 = 6 m and AM = 12 × √3/2 = 6√3 m. Thus NE = BM = 6 m. The horizontal distance from B to the building is BN = ME = AM + AE = 6√3 + 24 m. Since the angle of elevation from B to C is 45°, right triangle BNC has CN = BN = 6√3 + 24 m. Therefore CE = CN + NE = 6√3 + 24 + 6 = 6√3 + 30 m. Separately, in right triangle ADE, AE = 24 m and angle DAE = 53°, so DE = AE·tan53° ≈ 24 × 4/3 = 32 m. The billboard height is CD = CE − DE = 6√3 + 30 − 32 = 6√3 − 2. Using √3 ≈ 1.73, CD ≈ 6 × 1.73 − 2 = 8.38 ≈ 8.4 m.
